industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, with the sector rows carrying the view: Utilities integrated moves to Overweight this week on the first European power-price reading in a month (Nordic power forwards up, Fortum's 22-year nuclear agreement with Google; Danske Bank, 28 October), Regulated networks stays Neutral and Renewable generators stays Underweight because the ten-year above 5% is the row's discount rate. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: D now, D prior, DISAGREES with the sector move; rate-sensitives lagged on the week (Outset Global). Counter-case for B: pricing-power defensives are the rotation's destination; for D: the tape. Moves to B if a second power-price reading arrives with the industry's relative strength leaving D.

sector.why: Overweight, from Neutral, because the condition written on this row fired: a European power-price reading that supports the generators arrived. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): Nordic power forwards have risen and Fortum signed a 22-year nuclear power purchase agreement with Google, Europe's first lifetime-extension nuclear deal (Danske Bank, 28 October), which is the energy shock reaching contracted European power at long tenor; Jefferies' power analyst (28 October) raised the 2027 US data-centre build to about 27 gigawatts on satellite checks, and the defensive case at the level is unchanged (pricing-power defensives favoured). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: D now, C prior, DISAGREES: rate-sensitives lagged on the week (Outset Global, 29 October) and the market has not yet paid. One notch, not two, because the row is bond-proxy heavy with the ten-year above 5%. Five Pool names (PGE sixth on the starting score, leaving the Pool; Fortum, Endesa, Electrica, Public Power). Counter-case: one house, one deal and a forwards move with no number; the ten-year is the row's discount rate. Back to C if Nordic forwards fall back or relative strength falls to F; to A on a second power-price reading with relative strength leaving D.

geography.why: Neutral, carried, with the evidence for Underweight named and judged thin. Goldman Sachs (16 Oct) names 'worrying debt dynamics' in Austria alongside France, Belgium, Austria and Finland; that is one clause in one note with no spread reading, the same footing on which Ireland was held Neutral last week for Overweight, so the row does not move on it. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43). Relative strength is not graded by country. Moves to D if a second source names Austria or a spread reading is read widening.
